+++ lib/content-type-parser.js
@@ -151,7 +151,7 @@
     // next content type and match inconsistently. Reset it before testing.
     parserRegExp.lastIndex = 0
     if (parserRegExp.test(ct)) {
-      parser = this.customParsers.get(parserRegExp.toString())
+      parser = this.customParsers.get(parserRegExp)
       this.cache.set(ct, parser)
       return parser
     }

proposal.summary: In the `getParser` method, when a RegExp parser is matched, the code retrieves the parser using `parserRegExp.toString()` as the key, but the parser was stored with the actual RegExp object as the key in `customParsers`. This causes the lookup to fail and return undefined, leading to incorrect parser selection.
